Reference points with growth morphs from steepness and unfished recruitment

Source: R/gtg.R
gtg_brp.Rd

Fmsy, Bmsy, MSY and B0 of the growth-morph equilibrium, for a Beverton-Holt stock-recruitment relationship given by steepness h and unfished recruitment R0. Weight, maturity and effective selectivity at age change with F as fast growers are fished out, which equilibrium methods on a fixed selectivity at age miss (see build_om() with gtg).

Usage

gtg_brp(
  x,
  h = NULL,
  R0 = NULL,
  pattern = NULL,
  gtg = gtg_settings(),
  fbar_ages = NULL,
  spr_ref = 0.4
)

Arguments

x

a species spec (load_species()) or a floss_om built with gtg.

h

steepness. Default: the species' s; for an OM, its own SRR when h and R0 are both NULL.

R0

unfished recruitment (default 1, so biomass is per recruit). For an OM with h given and R0 = NULL, the OM's R0.

pattern

apical F by fleet (named vector; any scale). Default: the species' relq for a spec; the median fleet F of the last three years for an OM.

gtg

morph settings (gtg_settings()), used for a species spec.

fbar_ages

ages over which effective F is averaged for Fmsy (default 1 to tmax - 1, as in FLOSS OMs; for an OM, its fbar range).

spr_ref

SPR of the SPR-based proxy (default 0.4).

Value

an FLPar with Fmsy (on the fbar scale, effective F), Bmsy, MSY, B0, BmsyB0, SPRmsy, Fspr and Bspr (at spr_ref), h, R0, and the apical F of each fleet at MSY (Fmsy_<fleet>). For a species spec, weights are in kg (FLOSS specs give g), so biomass is in tonnes when R0 is in thousands.

Details

The relationship R = a S / (b + S) follows from h and R0 with the unfished spawning biomass per recruit phi0 of the morphs: B0 = R0 phi0, a = 4 h R0 / (5 h - 1), b = B0 (1 - h) / (5 h - 1). F is moved along the fleet pattern p (apical F by fleet, scaled to sum to 1): F_f = x p_f.

Examples

if (FALSE) {
sp <- load_species("siganus_sutor")
gtg_brp(sp, h = 0.7, R0 = 1000)
gtg_brp(sp, h = 0.7, pattern = c(traps = 1, gillnet = 0, linefish = 0))   # traps only
}
